articles.title: Singapore unveils new initiatives to help companies harness AI, such as to develop new products - The Straits Times
articles.summary: Singapore unveils new initiatives to help companies harness AI, such as to develop new products  The Straits Times
articles.full_text:
SINGAPORE – Singapore launched four new initiatives to support companies of all sizes in boosting their capability to implement and scale artificial intelligence, and use the technology to transform their businesses.
The initiatives reflect Singapore’s recognition that AI will rapidly become the defining force behind the next wave of innovation, transforming how new ideas, products and services are developed and commercialised.
Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong announced the initiatives at the 2026 Singapore Week of Innovation and Technology (SWITCH) on Oct 27, noting that Singapore will explore ways to make AI work better for its industries and workers, to build an economy that is more innovative, competitive and inclusive.
“AI offers opportunities to raise productivity, and develop new products and capabilities,” he said in his speech at the event’s opening ceremony held at Marina Bay Sands.
The initiatives follow the four national AI missions – advanced manufacturing, finance, healthcare and connectivity – announced by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong during Budget 2026.
Led by Enterprise Singapore (EnterpriseSG) in partnership with other Government agencies, the new initiatives include a Champions of AI programme to help ambitious Singapore-based companies committed to making AI a core driver of growth.
Dubbed by EnterpriseSG as the national flagship AI initiative, the programme will begin with a cohort of 24 companies across various industries, with more companies progressively coming on board.
The list of champions includes well-known local names such as DBS, OCBC, UOB, ST Engineering, Seatrium, PSA International, Singapore Airlines, Singtel Singapore, Keppel and Sembcorp.
The agency will work closely with these companies to develop tailored, long-term AI transformation road maps and provide them with access to curated AI expertise and solution providers, supporting enterprise-wide deployment of AI and change management, as well as workforce redesign and upskilling.
The second initiative is a series of agentic AI workshops to provide hands-on guidance to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) for adopting and scaling AI solutions.
Agentic AI is an artificial intelligence system that can accomplish a specific goal with limited supervision. It consists of AI agents, or machine learning models that mimic human decision-making to solve problems in real time.
The workshops will enable micro-entrepreneurs and small business owners to start their AI journey, identify practical use cases and build working prototypes tailored to their own businesses.
In the pilot run, more than 280 small businesses were supported to apply agentic AI tools in areas such as marketing, sales and customer service.
More workshops will be rolled out next month and scaled further in 2027.
The third initiative, termed Catalytic AI Solutions, aims to advance sector-wide AI adoption, starting with the advanced manufacturing, trade, and logistics sectors.
This initiative will help advanced manufacturers tackle key operational challenges and boost workflows, rice importers make smarter procurement and inventory management decisions, and logistic firms optimise routing decisions and allocating jobs across their fleet.
Perhaps the most ambitious of the four initiatives is MARVEL-AI, which stands for Accelerating Advanced Materials Innovation through AI and Automation.
Advanced materials are substances intentionally engineered, modified, or synthesised to exhibit novel or significantly enhanced physical and chemical properties. These deliver superior performance, structural strength, durability, and sustainability compared to traditional metals, ceramics or polymers.
These engineered materials act as the baseline enabling agents for industries – such as semiconductors, advanced manufacturing, energy and chemicals – and allow breakthroughs that are physically impossible with conventional inputs.
While newer materials can unlock better products, each material candidate has to go through a lengthy R&D process of experimentation, characterisation, validation, process development and industrial translation.
This can involve multiple development cycles, substantial resources and separate hand-offs between research and downstream development.
MARVEL-AI is designed to change the speed and scale of materials innovation, with a differentiated proposition that connects AI-enabled materials discovery, experimentation and validation with the pathway towards real-world industrial applications.
The initiative is likely to put Singapore on the map of advanced materials innovation – an area of intense competition among a handful of countries, including the US, Britain, China, Japan, South Korea and Switzerland.
Led by A*STAR, the initiative is supported by the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry, EnterpriseSG, Singapore Economic Development Board and National Research Foundation.
The initiative received initial funding of $150 million from the Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2030 (RIE2030), Singapore’s five-year $37 billion science and innovation masterplan announced in 2025.
MARVEL-AI is focused on four materials classes: metal alloys, polymers and organics, ceramics, and composites.
It also aims to create high-value start-ups, anchor large multinationals with materials development mandates and uplift local enterprises with frontier technologies.
Gan, who is also the Minister for Energy, Trade and Industry (Trade), said AI models such as Google’s Project GNoME (Graph Networks for Materials Exploration) and Microsoft’s MatterGen have shown the potential of AI to accelerate materials discovery.
He said the AI models will identify promising materials and design experiments, while the highly automated A*STAR laboratories will rapidly synthesise and test them.
“This will create opportunities for industry partnerships, enterprise growth and new ventures. We will also develop talent with capabilities spanning materials science, AI and automation, creating good job opportunities.
“Together, these efforts can deepen our industrial capabilities, develop new sources of growth, and strengthen Singapore’s position in advanced materials innovation,” he said.

articles.title: Myanmar woman asks Denmark to investigate alleged war crimes - The Star
articles.summary: Myanmar woman asks Denmark to investigate alleged war crimes  The Star
articles.full_text:
COPENHAGEN: A Myanmar citizen residing in Denmark on Monday (Oct 26) filed a complaint with Danish authorities against Myanmar's ruling military junta for alleged war crimes committed against minorities.
The complainant, Ngun Siang Dim, who is from the Chin minority, claims she saw 40 houses burn down in her village in Chin State, in western Myanmar, and that several members of her family and friends were killed or left permanently disabled by landmines laid by the junta.
The military junta "has done so many things", the 39-year-old said.
She said that children can no longer go to school, "and also because of the jet fighters, they keep (dropping) bombs, so they destroy our houses. So they have tortured a lot emotionally too".
Like thousands of others, she fled Myanmar, first to India and then Thailand, and has lived in Denmark since 2023.
AFP was not able to confirm the dates when the alleged events took place.
Other Myanmar citizens living in Denmark could join the complaint, which allows Danish police "to start up an investigation on potential international crimes and human rights violations committed against our clients and also communities in Myanmar", Eddie Khawaja, a lawyer representing the complainant and other Myanmar refugees, noted.
"This is truly a very important step in being able to tell this story, not only for her, but also in order to denounce the crimes that the military regime is committing against its own population," Tracy Bawi Hlei, president of Myanmar Action Group Denmark, stressed.
Since 2025, Denmark has adopted the principle of universal jurisdiction, allowing for the prosecution of war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocide. The principle permits judgment of such alleged crimes regardless of where they were committed, as long as the complainant or the alleged perpetrator is in Denmark.
Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing ousted the elected government of Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi in February 2021, plunging Myanmar into a civil war that has killed more than 100,000 people, according to monitor ACLED.
In early February, the Chin Human Rights Organisation announced that East Timor had appointed a prosecutor tasked with investigating a war crimes case allegedly committed by the Myanmar junta. - AFP

articles.title: Vietnam’s certificate of deposit rates keep rising - The Star
articles.summary: Vietnam’s certificate of deposit rates keep rising  The Star
articles.full_text:
HANOI: While savings interest rates have shown signs of cooling down, the rates on certificates of deposit (CDs) have kept rising by 0.1 to 0.3 percentage points per year.
Following the State Bank of Vietnam’s deposit rate cut directive last week, 20 banks have lowered their over-the-counter savings rates for six-month terms by 0.5 percentage points from the Oct 16 level.
However, the interest rates for CDs have continued to rise.
MB Bank is offering a rate of up to 8% per annum on three-month CDs for deposits of 300 million Vietnamese dong or more, 3.25 percentage points higher than the rate for a standard savings account of the same term. For deposits of one billion Vietnamese dong or more, the annual rate can reach 9.4%.
Similarly, VPBank is offering CD rates of up to 9% per annum, while BVBank provides a maximum rate of 8.2% per annum for terms ranging from six to 12 months.
The high CD rates showed that competitive pressure to attract capital remains, even as the general level of savings interest rates trends downward.
Truong Dac Nguyen, founder of investment firm Truong Nguyen, noted diverging interest rate trends across various deposit products.
While interest rates for standard savings accounts have edged downward, rates for other channels have continued to rise, signalling that banks remain driven by a need to secure capital, even at a higher cost.
Echoing this view, experts at SSI Research anticipated that the issuance of CDs and bonds will continue to accelerate, serving as an additional tool to help narrow the gap between credit growth and deposit mobilisation.
This shift indicated that banks are increasingly raising capital through longer-term instruments, which can help stabilise their funding bases and support the expansion of medium- and long-term credit.
However, a heavy reliance on CDs, particularly those with longer tenors, could also drive up the cost of capital if the issuance rates exceed those of conventional deposit products. — Viet Nam News/ANN

articles.title: Blame game erupts between Jakarta and provinces as Indonesia fires rage - The Straits Times
articles.summary: Blame game erupts between Jakarta and provinces as Indonesia fires rage  The Straits TimesSee more headlines and perspectives on Google News
articles.full_text:
AI generated
JAKARTA – A blame game has erupted between some of Indonesia’s provincial authorities and the central government as forest fires scorch Kalimantan and Sumatra.
Central Kalimantan’s administration under Governor Agustiar Sabran, pressed by Jakarta to step up firefighting, has publicly complained that forest concession permits are issued by the central government, while the provincial authorities and residents are left to deal with the fires.
Similar complaints have not been publicly voiced by provincial leaders in Sumatra.
Since the 2020 Job Creation Law centralised licensing powers, authority over business activities in forest areas has rested largely with Jakarta.
The row has now spilt onto the streets, with protest rallies held by the students of a few universities in Central Kalimantan, piling further pressure on the local government.
On Oct 19, a female university student led a protest outside the governor’s office in Palangka Raya, where she urged Agustiar to take bolder measures, including pressing the central government to declare the fires a national disaster. A TikTok video of the protest, with 26,000 likes and 888 comments as at the morning of Oct 20, has since circulated widely.
“We have suffered greatly for more than four months,” she said at the gate of the office.
She then mocked a banner that read: “Central Kalimantan free of haze 2026. Preventing forest fires starts with us”, emphasising that both the provincial and central governments had been warned about the intensity of this year’s El Nino since February, but failed to take action.
Agustiar listened calmly, surrounded by his deputies, aides and police officers, but did not respond. He promised to return to answer the protesters after praying, but he never reappeared, angering the students.
The protesters’ demands went to the heart of the dispute. Among them was a call for provincial governments to regain the power to revoke companies’ concession permits. However, this would be a long, drawn-out process through Parliament and unlikely to succeed.
In September 2026, Joni Harta, head of Central Kalimantan’s environment agency, said in a video posted on Instagram that drew 55,000 likes and more than 5,000 comments: “When the forest burns, why is Central Kalimantan province told to put out the fire? Why are the people of Central Kalimantan told to put it out? Not a single permit in forest areas was issued by the province. Should we be the ones putting it out?”
“Don’t pass the buck and blame my governor whenever something happens,” he added.
Joni also urged the Forestry Ministry to release funds owed to the province under the revenue-sharing scheme for a reforestation fund. “That money is our right. The central government should not hold it back,” he said.
His agency, he said, had done what it could within its responsibilities, putting up banners and campaigning against land burning. “We monitor companies that got permits from the central government but have no firefighting equipment, and we will certainly sanction them. But our budget is not enough.”
He added that the agency, and the Environment Ministry, were dealing with seven errant companies.
Jakarta pushes back
The Forestry Ministry has pushed back, insisting that fire prevention and control are shared responsibilities.
Responding to Joni’s remarks, the ministry’s public relations chief, Ristianto Pribadi, said on Sept 23 that fire management is a joint undertaking of the central and regional governments, law enforcement, businesses and communities, with authority determined by where a fire occurs, the status of the land, the type of business and the permits held.
He noted that environmental approvals for companies and their supervision fall to the Environment Ministry or provincial environment agencies, depending on their respective powers, a role that includes Joni’s own office. He said the Forestry Ministry oversees permit holders’ compliance in forest areas, including their fire-control obligations.
Putra Saptian, a senior campaigner at peatland-focused non-governmental organisation Pantau Gambut, agreed, arguing that regional and provincial governments retain significant authority.
“The claim that all responsibility shifted to the central government in 2020 is regarded as a fallacy,” he told The Straits Times, pointing out that provinces continue to have the authority to designate which land any company with a concession is entitled to operate on, and that provinces continue to have the power to halt operations of companies that breach a law.
The ministry has also moved to show it is acting against companies. In September 2026, it revoked the permits of five companies in West, South and Central Kalimantan, covering concessions totalling 92,464ha. On Oct 20, it said it had imposed administrative sanctions on 32 companies over 12,926ha of burnt land across seven provinces, and was handling suspected criminal cases against 125 individuals and corporations.
Who is ultimately responsible?
The dispute raises questions about who is ultimately accountable for resolving fires in Indonesia, whose recurring haze crises have consequences far beyond its borders, particularly for Singapore and Malaysia.
Writing on news site Maklumat on Oct 18, Abdul Khalid Boyan, a social and political analyst at Universitas Arya Wangsa, argued that since the 2020 law moved forestry licensing to Jakarta, the permits that serve as the main tool of oversight are located in the capital, hundreds to thousands of kilometres away from areas where fires could potentially spark. That distance, he wrote, delays the detection of violations and allows each side to shift responsibility.
But he did not spare the regions, noting that permits were handed out freely amid local political interests before centralisation in 2020. The answer, he argued, lies not in choosing between Jakarta and the provinces, but in ensuring that whoever holds authority can be held to account.
And early detection and action are also key.
Haze-hit residents in Sumatra and Kalimantan are urging President Prabowo Subianto to replace police chiefs and territorial military commanders in regions where fires have spread out of control.
They argue that stopping small fires from becoming major blazes requires early detection and rapid intervention, and that only the police and military, with personnel deployed down to the village level, have the reach to do this effectively.
“The military and police have resources and people across provinces and regencies. They can carry out prevention,” Ponco Pramono, 46, owner of a shrimp paste noodle shop in Palembang, South Sumatra, told ST on Oct 16.
He added: “Previously (under then President Joko Widodo), we understood there was a policy that provincial police chiefs and regional military commanders would be replaced if fires in their areas spread out of control. That is no longer the policy now under President Prabowo.”
Adi Siswoyo, 43, a farmer in Banjarbaru, South Kalimantan, said: “A field police officer (during the Widodo administration) confided that he could do little during the dry season besides patrol and hunt for hot spots, because his superior feared being replaced.” Adi said it is no longer the case under Prabowo, who took office in October 2024.
But in a possible sign of change, during a visit to Riau on Aug 24, Prabowo praised the province’s military commander, Major General Agus Hadi Waluyo, and police chief Inspector-General Herry Heryawan, and promised both promotions if the fires there were brought to an end.

The Autumn Economic Forum 2026, taking place from October 26th to 29th in Ho Chi Minh City, addresses a strategic question: How can Vietnam transform opportunities for international cooperation into a genuine growth engine? The global economy is shifting as capital flows seek new destinations, technology changes, and production methods and supply chains are reorganized.
 These changes open up opportunities for deeper participation in global value chains, while also creating higher demands for competition. The capacity to adopt technology, the quality of human resources, and the ability to connect with partners are increasingly determining the position of each economy.
 For Vietnam, this requirement is even more urgent as it aims for GDP growth exceeding 10% annually, with the digital economy contributing 30% of GDP by 2030. Orientations towards institutional breakthroughs, science and technology , private sector development, and international integration are laying the foundation for transforming the growth model.
 Vietnam needs to improve its technological capabilities, develop domestic businesses, and participate in high value-added stages of the global production chain.
 In this process, Ho Chi Minh City has the advantage of becoming a hub connecting domestic and international resources. Contributing approximately 23.4% of the country's GDP, the city is expanding its development space based on industry, trade, finance, high technology, logistics, and seaports.
 When organized into effective linkages, these advantages will empower the city and expand its ability to participate in the global growth network. The challenge is to shift from attracting individual resources to connecting, coordinating, and utilizing them effectively.
 This is also the focus of the Autumn Economic Forum 2026 organized by the Ho Chi Minh City People's Committee, with the positioning of "The convergence of new global growth poles" and the theme "The spirit of cooperation in the new era".
 The event aims to expand policy dialogue, connect economic actors, and form new cooperation frameworks. In particular, the two main days are co-branded with the World Economic Forum (WEF), opening up opportunities for Vietnam to connect with a network of international experts, policymakers, and businesses.
 The forum's four pillars include the role of megacities, disruptive technologies and innovation ecosystems, new cooperation models, and the pioneering role of the private sector. These elements complement each other: megacities create interconnected spaces, technology enhances productivity, cooperation expands resources, and businesses bring innovations into production.
 However, technology struggles to create value if businesses lack the capacity to apply it; capital flows are unlikely to be channeled into projects without transparent institutions, appropriate infrastructure, and human resources. Therefore, an effective coordination mechanism is needed to transform opportunities into action.
 This spirit is concretized through the CEO 500 program connecting investment capital, technology, and finance; 16 thematic sessions on institutions, development models, artificial intelligence, advanced manufacturing, and human resources; along with activities showcasing technology, digital transformation , and green transformation.
 In particular, the high-level plenary session and the Dialogue Program with the Prime Minister of Vietnam opened up a space for exchange on development orientations and new cooperation frameworks. The activities were linked to bring practical business issues into policy dialogue, while also connecting technological solutions with investment and application needs.
 However, the value of the 2026 Autumn Economic Forum lies not only in the scale of delegates or the number of agreements announced, but in the potential for sustained cooperation after the event. Policy proposals, once considered, will continue to connect investment opportunities, and technological initiatives will be put into practice.
 This is an opportunity to shift from attracting resources to actively organizing and effectively utilizing them; from participating to enhancing one's position in the value chain. In a world undergoing transformation, competitive advantage lies not only in having abundant resources, but also in the ability to connect and transform those resources into sustainable development value.

“It is becoming increasingly important that credits, when they are being generated, result in beneﬁts that ﬂow through more widely,” said Mr Chia.
The issues of transparency and integrity are only going to become more important as the carbon market expands, he noted.
Under the Paris Agreement, countries are allowed to buy carbon credits to meet their national climate pledges.
This means that other than taking steps to cut emissions within their borders, such as by investing in renewable energy infrastructure, countries can purchase carbon credits generated elsewhere and count these savings towards their target.
Countries can either purchase these credits from another country through a bilateral agreement or buy them from a new carbon credit market administered by the UN. The mechanisms for this UN market are still being negotiated but could be ﬁnalised in the next year or two.
“You have credits generated by different registries, which are then transferred to maybe a private sector company, transferred to a country, and they move all over the place. Dr Tan spoke on the effectiveness of the Complementarity Assessment (COMPASS) framework as well.
COMPASS is a points-based framework that evaluates attributes of individual EP applicants and their prospective employer, in deciding to issue the pass.
All new EP applications made since 1 September 2023, have been evaluated through COMPASS, and the framework will be extended to renewals from 1 September 2024.
Under COMPASS, four “foundational” criteria are used to assess an application. They are an individual’s salary and qualifications, as well as the firm’s workforce diversity and support for local employment.
Bonus points are given to jobs where there is a lack of skilled workers specified on a Shortage Occupation List, and firms that partner the Government on ambitious innovation and internationalisation activities.
To pass the evaluation, which is designed to provide firms with greater clarity and certainty for manpower planning, the application needs to rack up 40 points.
Responding to labour MPs Patrick Tay (Pioneer) and Desmond Choo (Tampines GRC), Dr Tan said the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) has been engaging and supporting companies that score poorly on firm-related attributes under COMPASS, to help them improve their workforce profile and adjust to the framework.
He said more than 440 firms have attended TAFEP’s workshops over the past year.
Firms with unfair hiring practices will still be taken to task under the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices, and under upcoming workplace fairness legislation in future, he added.
Dr Tan also responded to questions from Leader of the Opposition Pritam Singh and Mr Choo on the effectiveness of the Shortage Occupation List in easing skills shortages.
He noted that the list was designed to award bonus points on COMPASS to EP applicants filling acute occupational shortages in areas of strategic importance for the economy.
Roles on the list include artificial intelligence engineer, carbon trader, and alternative protein food application scientist, among others.
The proportion of EP holders in shortage occupations has increased since COMPASS was implemented, which Dr Tan said shows the list reflects real shortages industries face.
He added that based on preliminary data since COMPASS’ implementation in September 2023, 20 per cent of new EP holders working in roles on the list used the bonus points to pass COMPASS.
“Therefore, the Shortage Occupation List is very helpful in ensuring that COMPASS does not hinder business growth because of a shortage of skills locally.”
However, he added that some occupations continue to have small numbers of EP holders, such as those in the green economy and agri-tech, which are very nascent fields globally.
“While we partner agencies in recruiting them here, we are also contemporaneously investing in developing our local talents for these jobs.”
Dr Tan also provided an update on the Overseas Networks and Expertise (ONE) Pass, launched in January 2023 to draw top talent to Singapore.
Almost 4,200 ONE Pass applications had been approved as at 1 January 2024, he said. He added: “In an era where talent is scarce, businesses follow talent.”

It was flying off the shelves, but what was less well-known about it was that it was a product of P&G’s Singapore Innovation Centre (SgIC) in Biopolis, Singapore’s research and development (R&D) hub for biomedical science.
The SgIC is the consumer goods giant’s largest beauty innovation hub in Asia. The 32,000-square-metre facility handles consumer understanding, formulation, advanced analytical capabilities, data science and modelling, along with state-of-the-art packaging design.
The centre employs around 500 people, including scientists involved in R&D and product development for the giant’s beauty brands, which include Pantene, Head & Shoulders, SK-II, and Olay.
The Olay Super Serum was just one success story to come out of the innovation centre, which marked its 10th anniversary last year.
Major companies in Singapore such as Visa, Siemens, and ABB also have their own innovation centres, as the Republic is pushing innovation to the forefront and building an ecosystem to support it. Companies ranging from multinational firms to startups are choosing Singapore to create, test, and export their innovative solutions to Asia and beyond.

KAJANG: A man who was reported missing by his family five days ago was found dead in a car at a supermarket car park in Jalan Impian Mahkota last night.
District police chief assistant commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said police received a report about the discovery of the car at 11.29pm.
"Initial investigations found a man, believed to be in his 50s, lying unconscious in the driver's seat of a Perodua Axia.
"The engine was off and the car was locked from the inside," he said.
He said police sought the assistance of Fire and Rescue Department personnel to open the car door before medical personnel from Kajang Hospital examined the victim and pronounced him dead.
What To Read Next
He said police received a missing person report last Tuesday after the man's family members were unable to contact him.
"Preliminary investigations have so far found no foul play at the scene or on the deceased. The case has been classified as a sudden death report (SDR).
"Further investigations are ongoing to determine the cause of the incident and his death," he said in a statement today.
Those with information about the incident is urged to contact investigating officer Inspector Shisheewady Ruzani at 016-856 5670 or the nearest police station.
Earlier, several photographs went viral showing police and Fire and Rescue Department personnel examining a parked car near a supermarket.
Following this, several social media users claimed that the man inside the car was their family member who had been reported missing five days earlier and was found at the location.
The man and the car were found about 15 minutes from where he allegedly lived.

articles.title: Nine companies from Singapore and the region bag top honours at 2026 Emerging Enterprise Awards - The Business Times
articles.summary: Nine companies from Singapore and the region bag top honours at 2026 Emerging Enterprise Awards  The Business Times
articles.full_text:
More than a third of the 600 applications received this year came from Hong Kong, Indonesia and Malaysia
[SINGAPORE] Nine companies from Singapore, Malaysia, Hong Kong and Indonesia took top honours for their innovative and sustainable solutions at the 2026 Emerging Enterprise Awards on Monday (Oct 26) night.
Jointly organised by The Business Times and OCBC, the annual awards recognise young businesses for their entrepreneurial spirit, innovation and resilience. The awards, currently in its 19th edition, are open to businesses that are under 10 years old and have an annual turnover of up to S$20 million.
Close to 600 applications from a broad mix of industries were received this year. Applications from Hong Kong, Indonesia and Malaysia made up almost 40 per cent of the total, underscoring the growing regional appeal of the awards. A total of 28 companies were shortlisted as finalists.
Singapore-based Woosa Sleep and Hong Kong-based MediConCen received the Emerging Enterprise Award.
The category recognises emerging enterprises with enterprising mindsets that drive consistent, significant and sustainable growth. These businesses also display the ability to scale and expand outside their home markets.
Woosa Sleep is a Singapore-based sleep wellness company specialising in the design, manufacturing and direct-to-consumer sale of a range of premium mattresses, smart storage bed frames, adjustable bases and sleep-related lifestyle products tailored to the region’s tropical climate.
Hong Kong-based MediConCen develops and deploys an agentic artificial intelligence that fully automates the entire insurance claims process for insurers. Its solutions cover claims decisioning, real-time fraud detection, workflow automation and secure medical-network connectivity. The firm recently introduced an integrated payment solution with Mastercard that enables seamless claims-to-payment experiences.
In the Most Promising Start-up Award category, Hong Kong-headquartered Alpha AI Technology and Malaysia-based Hyperscale DCS were named winners.
The award recognises enterprises that demonstrate a strong startup spirit and have a unique and commercially viable idea with long-term potential.
Headquartered in Hong Kong, Alpha AI provides AI-powered inspection and asset-monitoring services that are sensor and platform-agnostic. Its customers include property and facility managers, developers, government agencies, utilities and operators of major structures. The firm is expanding its presence in South Korea and the Greater Bay Area in China.
Malaysia-based Hyperscale DCS is a specialist in data centre infrastructure focused on power, cooling and modular prefabricated systems. The company also operates across Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam and the United Kingdom.
“Diamonds”
The winners were honoured at an awards ceremony held at the JW Marriott Hotel Singapore South Beach on Monday, which was themed “Diamonds”.
In her speech at the event, guest of honour Senior Minister of State for Energy, Trade and Industry Low Yen Ling said the theme was an apt metaphor for award-winning enterprises, describing how they had “truly emerged as champions after an arduous growth journey” much like diamonds forming under tremendous pressure and polished to shine.
She said: “The path from the seed of bold ideas to scaling the rocks of challenges has brought enterprises to the pinnacle of success tonight.”
She noted that in recent years, companies have had to navigate a more complex and uncertain operating environment, ranging from geopolitical tensions and supply chain disruptions to rising business costs and changing consumer preferences.
“For emerging enterprises, all these pressures can be very daunting, given your relatively limited resources and the demands of scaling your businesses,” said Low, who is also Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth.
She added that resilient emerging enterprises are “not distinguished simply by the ability to withstand challenges, but also the willingness to adapt and find new ways to create value”.
That willingness to adapt was evident in the sustainability space. Low said she was “encouraged” that promising enterprises continue to vie for the Emerging Enterprise Sustainability Award as their ability to harness technology and innovation to develop clever solutions helps Singapore tackle climate impact and enhance its green sector.
This year, the award went to four companies: Singapore-based Matwerkz Technologies, Malaysia-based Geomax Rubber Innovative Products, Malaysia-based Lafre Global and Indonesia-based Parongpong Raw Lab.
Introduced in 2023, the award recognises emerging enterprises that are capitalising on growth opportunities in the green economy. These businesses embed sustainability in their operations while leveraging technology and new solutions to move towards low-carbon business models and industries.
Matwerkz Technologies develops thermal management, fire protection and functional materials technologies. Its flagship technology, Thermorphous, can improve battery performance and safety at the same time. The company has customers and partners across six key markets: Singapore, China, Japan, Malaysia, India and Europe.
Geomax Rubber Innovative Products uses patented recycling technology to turn rejected nitrile rubber gloves into value-added products. Its circular business model gives discarded materials a second life in products such as safety footwear, coasters and floor tiles.
Lafre Global is Malaysia’s first sanitary pad brand to introduce Braille packaging nationwide. The initiative addresses challenges faced by visually impaired women, who may have difficulty identifying and purchasing intimate care products independently. Lafre saids its sanitary pads also deliver 50 times the absorbency of conventional pads.
In Indonesia, Parongpong Raw Lab specialises in research, development and production focused on sustainability, the circular economy and material innovation.
Through its patent-pending Prototech technology, the company converts low-value waste – particularly discarded fishing nets – and other hard-to-recycle materials into higher-value products such as structural building materials.
Parongpong Raw Lab works directly with coastal fishing communities and informal waste collectors in Indonesia.
This year, the Most Promising Sustainability Start-up Award went to Singapore’s XEL Lifecare (AIRE). The award recognises enterprises with a commercially viable green or sustainability-related business model that has long-term potential and a strong startup spirit.
AIRE is a startup specialising in adult incontinence care. Its products, co-developed with seniors in Singapore, include adult pull-up pants, diapers and overnight variants.
The winners received their awards from Low at the ceremony. The two winners of the Emerging Enterprise Award, as well as the four winners of the Emerging Enterprise Sustainability Award, each received a two-year, interest-free term loan of up to S$200,000 and a business consulting package from RSM Singapore worth S$15,000.
All nine winners will also be featured across BT’s print, digital, social media, radio and podcast channels in Singapore and the region.
BT editor Chen Huifen said: “The journey from submission to shortlist and finalist has put these young enterprises through close scrutiny of their ideas, execution and potential for growth. While not every finalist will walk away with the top honours, standing among the final selection is an exceptional achievement in itself.”
That recognition matters all the more given the climate in which these businesses operate, said Christie Chu, head of emerging business international at OCBC. (* See amendment note)
“Young businesses today need more than access to capital to succeed,” she said. “They also require visibility, trusted networks, market access and the right ecosystem of support around them – all of which the EE Awards provide.”
“Over the years, Emerging Enterprise has become more than just an awards platform. It has grown into a community where entrepreneurs connect, collaborate and create new opportunities together. A conversation at an alumnus gathering created an opportunity for an entirely new business to be born, and that business went on to become an award winner itself,” said Elaine Heng, head of global commercial banking at OCBC.
The Emerging Enterprise 2026 Awards is supported by Mastercard, RSM - Singapore, the Agency for Science, Technology and Research, CBRE and Enterprise Singapore.
* Amendment note: The article has been updated to reflect Christie Chu’s current designation.

articles.title: Research and Technology Drive Indonesia's Industrial Development - Kompas.id
articles.summary: Research and Technology Drive Indonesia's Industrial Development  Kompas.id
articles.full_text:
Technological innovation in Indonesia faces challenges from geopolitical challenges and the advent of AI. In addition to requiring funding, human resource development needs to be strengthened.
26 Okt 2026 20:58 WIB · Sains & Teknologi
JAKARTA, KOMPAS - Indonesia's technological innovation must be backed by ongoing research and development amid shifting geopolitical landscapes and the rapid advancement of imitation technology. This effort is deemed crucial for driving industrialization and helping Indonesia escape the middle-income trap.
This issue was raised during the Danantara Technology Innovation Investment Forum (DTIIF) on its opening day at the Fairmont Hotel Jakarta on Monday (26/10/2026).
Bambang Permadi Soemantri Brodjonegoro, Dean and Chief Executive Officer of the Asian Development Bank Institute (ABDI), stated that the economic growth model in ASEAN countries must be based on technology adaptation, particularly through imitation intelligence or AI, to generate higher added value.
According to Bambang, geopolitical and geo-economic changes have transformed global trade, investment, and supply chains. In this context, Indonesia faces unique challenges in developing its industries and enhancing economic competitiveness.
Bambang believes that technological adaptation is necessary not only in the manufacturing sector but also in the agricultural and service sectors. These efforts must be supported by research and development (R&D) and innovation to add value to products and services.
The forum aims to connect various stakeholders, including universities, technology developers, and investors, to foster collaboration. Its primary goal is to facilitate the downstream commercialization of research and technology development.
"Even though we are far behind other countries in Asia, now is the right time for Indonesia to boost technological innovation through research and development," said Bambang.
Reza Yamora Siregar, Managing Director and Chief Economist of Danantara Indonesia, who also attended the forum, emphasized the importance of sustainable technological growth. He noted that Indonesia's energy and resources are significant advantages that can serve as a foundation for sustainable development.
This effort is primarily driven by the government's commitment to renewable energy, which is experiencing rapid growth. For instance, this swift expansion is evident in the increasing number of electric vehicles in Indonesia.
The development of digital hardware in Indonesia, including data centers, cloud computing, and e-commerce, also plays a significant role in Southeast Asia and Asia. Therefore, data centers are crucial as part of the infrastructure. Furthermore, he emphasized the need for cross-sector collaboration to foster innovation.
Bambang also emphasized the importance of leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) to facilitate the development of technology and industry. According to a World Bank report, the tangible impact of the internet and computer technology typically takes about one to two decades to materialize.
Conversely, the presence of AI has had a more rapid impact in less than a decade. Therefore, Bambang emphasized that society must prepare to coexist with this technology.
However, the challenges we face extend beyond the presence of artificial intelligence. Indonesia frequently encounters failures in technological innovation due to being trapped in a middle-income status. Therefore, there is a strong emphasis on the need for industrial revitalization aimed at producing higher value-added goods, with one key aspect being the industrialization of technology.
Bambang reiterated that deindustrialization in Indonesia is still in its early stages. The country frequently faces innovation failures due to being trapped in a middle-income status.
Previously, Indonesia experienced an economic infusion, successfully transitioning from primary sectors such as agriculture and mining to manufacturing. This achievement took place during the 1980s and early 1990s.
At that time, Indonesia experienced its highest economic growth of 8 percent in 1994-1995, driven by a shift to the manufacturing sector. However, this transformation was characterized by labor-intensive manufacturing.
Following the financial crisis in Asian countries, Indonesia also experienced premature industrialization. This crisis devastated parts of the manufacturing sector. Furthermore, deindustrialization occurred due to the boom in natural resource commodities.
"We suddenly seem to experience a kind of short-term amnesia about being an industrial nation, as Indonesia has abruptly shifted its focus to the oil and gas sector, particularly palm oil and coal," said Bambang.
Next, in 2001, there was a global shock when China joined the World Trade Organization (WTO).
This has affected competition in the global manufacturing industry, including for developing countries like Indonesia. The industrial chain has been impacted, not only in terms of products but also in the supply chain.
"That period made Indonesia never truly realize the manufacturing sector after the Asian financial crisis. How can we support Indonesia as a more industrialized nation?" he stated.
Bambang emphasized that increasing productivity through technology must go hand in hand with the transition to clean energy, without neglecting the affordability and reliability of electricity supply for industries.
He also highlighted Japan's renewed push for investment, particularly in data centers and artificial intelligence (AI), amid shifts in the global supply chain.
Bambang stated that the success of countries in avoiding the income trap, according to the World Bank's 2024 development report, is based on three factors: investment, funding injections, and innovation.
Investment will be crucial as our country remains low-income and seeks to elevate itself to a lower-middle-income level. Furthermore, as the economy transitions from middle-income to high-income status, the emphasis must shift to innovation.
Amid the crucial development of the industry and manufacturing sectors, Finance Minister Suahasil Nazara, who also attended the forum, emphasized the importance of human resource development.
Suahasil stated that Indonesia has two main strengths: its people and its natural resources. He outlined five key actions that the country must consistently undertake, with the first being the development of human resources.
"Everything we do, from the State Budget (APBN) to non-APBN initiatives, involves raising funds for the community in the education and health sectors," he stated.
Suahasil stated that the Ministry of Finance's largest expenditures are on providing food and education. This is because social infrastructure, in the form of human resource development, is a fundamental requirement. If citizens' physical and spiritual needs are met and they are free from stunting, this will support other development initiatives.
In addition, Suahasil emphasized the importance of infrastructure development. While infrastructure projects do not need to be entirely funded by the government, the state plays a crucial role in their provision. Furthermore, strengthening institutions is essential for achieving good, dynamic, and equitable governance.
"Structural reform is about how we work and the interconnections between one institution and another," Suahasil emphasized. He also stressed the importance of maintaining stability as part of sustainable economic development.

articles.title: AEF 2026: Enabling the global business community to view Ho Chi Minh City with a new perspective. - Vietnam.vn

This is the annual conference program of the Autumn Economic Forum, bringing together more than 500 business leaders to explore collaboration opportunities and new growth initiatives for Ho Chi Minh City.
 If the Forum's overarching theme focused on convergence at the macro level, CEO500 brought that spirit down to the most specific level: the convergence of FDI, technology, and international financial flows—factors that are reshaping the global investment landscape.
 Attending the program were Mr. Nguyen Loc Ha, Standing Vice Chairman of the People's Committee of Ho Chi Minh City; Mr. Nguyen Cong Vinh, Vice Chairman of the People's Committee of Ho Chi Minh City; representatives from the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs; as well as representatives from international ministries, sectors, and localities from Bangladesh, India , Mongolia, Japan, the United States, Australia, etc.; and many diplomatic missions and international organizations in Vietnam...
 A gateway connecting Vietnam to technology capital, markets, and development resources. 
|  | 
| Vice Chairman of Ho Chi Minh City People's Committee Nguyen Cong Vinh delivered a welcoming speech and officially opened the CEO500 program. (Photo: Thanh Long) | 
 In his welcoming remarks, Vice Chairman of the Ho Chi Minh City People's Committee Nguyen Cong Vinh affirmed that the CEO 500 program, themed "The Convergence of FDI, Technology, and Global Financial Flows," is a very special dialogue that not only helps attract more investment capital, but more importantly, allows investors to recognize new opportunities and requirements; to jointly solve specific development problems and create new opportunities and growth drivers, especially in the context of the boom in science and technology and the need to connect global capital flows.
 According to him, Ho Chi Minh City is entering a new development space. After the merger, the city's economic, urban, and connectivity space has expanded, creating more room for large-scale projects; along with resolutions that open up a groundbreaking institutional framework for the city named after President Ho Chi Minh, with strong decentralization and greater delegation of power in planning and resource mobilization.
 Simultaneously, amidst increasingly fierce competition to attract international investment, Ho Chi Minh City prioritizes high-quality FDI flows, focusing on finance, technology, digital transformation , green economy, sustainable development, and innovation; determined to implement the plan and strive to achieve the target of attracting $19 billion in foreign investment in 2026. 
|  | 
| Overview of the program. (Photo: Jackie Chan) | 
 In that spirit, Vice Chairman of the People's Committee Nguyen Cong Vinh stated that the program focuses on four key drivers of the city's development:
 Firstly , there is the development of new infrastructure and space. The city is ready to work with investors on each project: Transport-Oriented Development (TOD), seaports, logistics, and free trade zones.
 Secondly, there's the financial aspect. The International Finance Centre in Ho Chi Minh City is a driving force connecting the city with regional capital flows and financial markets. We invite international financial institutions to clarify the conditions, procedures, and roadmap for joining the centre right from the outset.
 Third is energy. As urban areas, industries, and logistics expand, a clean and stable energy source becomes a prerequisite for all investment decisions. The city hopes to work with investors to select the appropriate model, priority areas, and implementation roadmap.
 Fourth is the digital economy and technology. Science, technology, and innovation are decisive drivers of growth, with strategic data infrastructure, artificial intelligence, high-tech zones, and controlled testing mechanisms. The city invites technology corporations to jointly select priority testing areas so that technologies can be tested, applied, and expanded from Ho Chi Minh City to larger markets.
 “The city is ready to listen, receive specific proposals, and work with the business community to solve practical problems in the spirit of ‘clear tasks, clear responsibilities, and clear timelines.’ We hope today will be an opportunity for the global business community to view Ho Chi Minh City with a new perspective,” Mr. Nguyen Cong Vinh expressed; while emphasizing that Ho Chi Minh City is not only a large market of Vietnam but is also aiming to become a gateway connecting Vietnam with technology, markets, and development resources for the entire region and the world .
 From here, businesses can access the Vietnamese market, connect with manufacturing, logistics, finance, and technology centers, and expand their operations into a broader economic space. The city proactively facilitates connections so that actively flowing capital can meet new technologies, markets, human resources, and development opportunities.
 Enhance resilience 
|  | 
| Mr. Fazurin Jamaludin, Head of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) Representative Office in Vietnam and Laos, speaks at the event. (Photo: Thanh Long) | 
 Meanwhile, Fazurin Jamaludin, Head of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) Representative Office in Vietnam and Laos, emphasized that financial and investment flows can only remain stable in the long term when secured by solid macroeconomic foundations and sustainable growth.
 Accordingly, the global economy has demonstrated better-than-expected resilience, despite facing numerous shocks and crises in 2026. Although growth has slowed, the world economy has maintained its resilience thanks to several factors, including reduced reliance on energy and the adaptability of economies.
 Regarding the Asia-Pacific region, Fazurin Jamaludin noted that economies have demonstrated the ability to adapt flexibly to energy supply disruptions. Although the region is significantly dependent on oil from the Middle East, for much of 2026, economies reduced fuel imports from that region and increased imports from other sources. Total fuel imports also decreased compared to 2025.
 Furthermore, Asian economies are benefiting from the spillover effects of the AI-driven technology growth cycle, through manufacturing, industrial production, and related services. This wave is boosting exports of technology products and contributing to increased intra-regional trade in both technology and non-technology sectors. Investment in technology surged in the first half of 2026, far exceeding the total investment for the entire year of 2025. As a result, the economic performance of many countries has been more positive than expected.
 Furthermore, addressing solutions to strengthen the macroeconomic foundation and maintain investment flows, the IMF Representative in Vietnam and Laos affirmed that Vietnam in general and Ho Chi Minh City in particular need to ensure solid macroeconomic conditions so that investment flows can remain stable and sustainable in the long term.
 First, in the context of increasing inflationary pressure, Vietnam needs to prioritize price stability in its monetary policy management. At the same time, countries also need to preserve fiscal space to have sufficient resources to respond to further shocks. Support measures should be designed with clear objectives and be temporary in nature, ensuring that resources reach those in need without undermining the sustainability of the budget. 
|  | 
| Permanent Vice Chairman of the Ho Chi Minh City People's Committee Nguyen Loc Ha and Vice Chairman of the Ho Chi Minh City People's Committee Nguyen Cong Vinh attended the event. (Photo: Thanh Long) | 
 In the medium term, Fazurin Jamaludin argues that countries need to address structural issues, including adjusting labor policies to prepare the workforce for the changes brought about by AI, strengthening social security systems, and enhancing energy security through cooperation among nations.
 Furthermore, regional integration and cooperation need to be further promoted. According to IMF analysis, trade in services within ASEAN has not yet reached a high level of integration. Countries can strengthen cooperation and remove barriers to trade in services to expand regional exchanges, thereby supporting economic growth.
 Specifically for Vietnam, Mr. Fazurin Jamaludin believes that there are still some structural issues that need to be prioritized for addressing in order to improve the economic foundation and enhance the quality of growth.
 Firstly , Vietnam needs to improve its total factor productivity (TFP).
 Secondly , Vietnam needs to continue modernizing its macroeconomic policy framework, including monetary and fiscal policies, thereby strengthening the long-term reliability of the economy.
 Thirdly , it is necessary to improve the quality of economic data and enhance the provision of information to the market. Despite Vietnam's rapid economic growth, its capacity to meet data demands and provide information remains limited. Addressing these data gaps will help investors and stakeholders better assess the situation, prospects, and potential of the Vietnamese economy, thereby enabling them to make informed decisions and increase investment in the market.
 Finally, Mr. Fazurin Jamaludin expressed that strengthening macroeconomic foundations, promoting structural reforms, enhancing productivity, and improving data quality are crucial tasks for Vietnam to enhance its resilience to shocks, capitalize on opportunities arising from global economic shifts, and maintain sustainable long-term investment flows.

HÀ NỘI — Benchmark indices retreated on Monday, as widespread selling in banking and securities stocks dragged down the VN-Index, while market liquidity fell from the previous session.
The VN-Index on the Hochiminh Stock Exchange (HoSE) lost 10.6 points to close at 1,763.55 points. The reversal ended the index's rising streak over the previous four sessions.
It briefly climbed above 1,780 points during the morning session before selling pressure intensified towards midday and continued into the afternoon, weighing on the broader market.
The southern market's breadth was negative, as 205 stocks declined while 106 ticker symbols inched higher. Liquidity decreased nearly 22 per cent from Friday's trade to VNĐ13.5 trillion (US$523 million).
Banking stocks, often regarded as the market's leading group, faced broad-based declines. Eximbank (EIB) fell 3.92 per cent, followed by VPBank (VPB), down 2.07 per cent, Sahabank (SHB), down 1.83 per cent, and VIB, down 1.76 per cent.
HDBank (HDB) dropped 1.55 per cent, Sacombank (STB) lost 1.31 per cent, MBBank (MBB) fell 1.26 per cent, and Vietcombank (VCB) declined 1.23 per cent. Techcombank (TCB) slipped 1.17 per cent, VietinBank (CTG) lost 1.13 per cent, and BIDV (BID) fell 1.46 per cent.
The declines came as deposit interest rates were being adjusted in line with directives from the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV).
Securities stocks also performed poorly, adding to the downward pressure on the benchmark.
Saigon - Hanoi Securities (SHS) and Tien Phong Securities (ORS) each fell 3.13 per cent, while Vietcap Securities (VCI) declined 2.3 per cent. VIX Securities (VIX) lost 1.57 per cent, VNDirect Securities (VND) fell 1.45 per cent and SSI Securities (SSI) slipped 0.75 per cent.
Real estate stocks were also predominantly lower. Dat Xanh Group (DXG) fell 3.35 per cent, Vincom Retail (VRE) declined 2.8 per cent, Development Investment Construction (DIG) lost 1.97 per cent, Vinhomes (VHM) slipped 0.62 per cent and Novaland (NVL) edged down 0.47 per cent.
Vingroup (VIC) moved against the trend, rising 0.21 per cent, while Viglacera (VGC) gained 4.04 per cent and Vietjet Air (VJC) advanced 1.77 per cent.
Energy stocks, meanwhile, largely maintained their positive momentum. PetroVietnam Refining and Petrochemical (BSR) rose 1.2 per cent, while Petrolimex (PLX) and PetroVietnam Gas (GAS) each gained 0.56 per cent. PV Drilling (PVD) edged up 0.27 per cent.
Foreign investors continued to add pressure on the market. They net sold VNĐ892 billion on HoSE and VNĐ300 million on HNX.
FPT Corporation (FPT) was the most heavily net-sold stock by foreign investors, with net sales worth approximately VNĐ258 billion. — BIZHUB/VNS

The policy of reducing lending interest rates is expected to help businesses lower capital costs, recover production, and expand their operations. However, for many small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), the difficulties lie not only in interest rates but also in access to capital, credit limits, and the pressure to maintain cash flow.
Businesses have factories and orders, but they worry about losing cash flow.
At the conference "Banking Sector Accompanying and Unlocking Financial and Banking Resources to Serve Growth in the Southeast Region in the Period 2026-2030" held on October 23rd, Governor of the State Bank of Vietnam Pham Duc An outlined the direction to reduce lending interest rates by 1.5-2% for production, business, and priority sectors. This move opens up expectations for lower-cost capital, supporting businesses to maintain operations and creating momentum for economic growth.
Many banks continue to lower interest rates following strong directives from the Government and the State Bank of Vietnam to support businesses and individuals in their production and business activities.
However, there is still a gap between the policy of reducing interest rates and the actual accessibility of capital. For many small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), the important thing is not just the interest rate, but also whether they can borrow capital at all, whether the loan limit meets their needs, and whether they have sufficient cash flow to maintain production and business operations.
Mr. Duong Thanh Dao, General Director of Hai Dao Food Company, said that businesses welcome the policy of reducing interest rates in the context of a volatile economy. However, according to him, what businesses expect is not just the announced reduction in interest rates, but the actual flow of capital into production activities.
A unique characteristic of the seafood industry is that businesses must advance capital to purchase raw materials, process, preserve, and transport them. Meanwhile, customers typically pay their debts after 40-60 days, or even longer. Until the payment is received, businesses still have to pay for raw materials, employee salaries, electricity, cold storage, logistics, and loan interest.

A prolonged capital turnover cycle creates increasing financial pressure, especially when profit margins are strained by input costs and market competition. Even a few percent increase in financial costs can significantly erode a company's accumulated profits.
"The announced reduction in interest rates is a positive sign, but what's more important is whether businesses can actually borrow capital at a reasonable interest rate," Mr. Dao shared.
In reality, Hai Dao Food's challenges lie in capital costs and the ability to maintain credit limits. In 2025, with the desire to develop production, improve processing capacity, and expand the market, the company invested in building a factory and simultaneously mobilized personal loans to supplement investment and business activities.
According to Mr. Dao, due to the specific nature of collateral assets, especially agricultural land, accessing credit under the corporate legal entity model faces many obstacles. After the factory is invested in, banks conduct reassessments and narrow credit limits, sometimes reducing them by about 50% compared to before. At the same time, businesses face pressure from loans coming due.

Capital has been invested in the factory, goods, and accounts receivable from customers, but the need for cash to maintain production continues to arise. When credit limits are tightened, businesses have to find ways to raise funds to purchase raw materials, pay salaries, make payments to suppliers, and fulfill their obligations to the bank.
"High interest rates are already difficult, but having credit limits tightened when businesses desperately need capital is even more dangerous," Mr. Dao said.
According to the business leader, banks have a responsibility to manage risk, but assessing debt repayment capacity should also take into account cash flow, output contracts, business history, and payment ability, rather than relying too heavily on the value of collateral.
Based on practical experience, Mr. Dao suggested that interest rate reductions should be accompanied by improved access to capital, especially for SMEs in manufacturing, agriculture, fisheries, and export sectors. Banks also need a suitable roadmap when adjusting credit limits, avoiding sudden capital shortages for businesses in the middle of their production cycles.
Businesses desire access to order-based, supply chain-based, accounts receivable-based, and inventory-based financing options under suitable conditions; and the development of credit guarantee mechanisms to support entities with viable business plans but limited collateral.
"We don't seek loans at any cost, nor do we expect banks to bear the business risks for us. What businesses need is a proper assessment of their capabilities, fair access to capital, and time to adapt when credit policies change," Mr. Dao emphasized.
Lowering interest rates is necessary but not sufficient.
Analyzing the significance of interest rate reductions, Associate Professor Dr. Dinh Trong Thinh, an economic expert, believes that banks lowering interest rates in line with the government and State Bank's directives can help reduce borrowing costs, thereby easing debt repayment pressure and creating favorable conditions for businesses to recover and expand production and business activities.
When capital costs decrease, businesses have more financial space to invest in machinery, replenish raw materials, maintain jobs, and enhance competitiveness. On a broader scale, capital channeled into efficient production will contribute to supporting economic growth.
However, according to experts, lowering interest rates is not the only solution to alleviate difficulties for businesses. In a context where many businesses are still facing order shortages, high input costs, and weak market demand, reducing borrowing costs only addresses part of the problem.

If output does not improve, goods are difficult to sell, and cash flow is stagnant, then even with lower interest rates, businesses may still struggle to repay debts and maintain operations. Therefore, production and business activities need to be prepared in a coordinated manner, keeping pace with market trends and operating within a clear and stable legal framework.
Furthermore, lowering interest rates to ensure capital flows into the economy is not a simple task. According to Associate Professor Dr. Dinh Trong Thinh, the State Bank of Vietnam needs to continue to flexibly utilize monetary policy tools, improve the effectiveness of liquidity support channels, including short-term lending tools with appropriate interest rates, creating conditions for a sustainable reduction in capital costs while ensuring the safety of the credit system.
From the perspective of commercial banks, the challenge is to balance risk management requirements with the actual capital needs of businesses. Credit assessment needs to consider the overall financial resources, cash flow, product sales capacity, and debt repayment history. For businesses with genuine production activities, output contracts, and viable business plans, appropriate financing mechanisms can contribute to improving access to capital.
At the same time, businesses themselves need to proactively improve their financial management capabilities, control costs, develop cash flow plans, and choose production methods that suit market demand. Low-cost capital is only effective when used for the right purposes, generating sufficient revenue and cash flow to sustain operations and fulfill debt repayment obligations.
Therefore, the effectiveness of interest rate reduction policies should not only be judged by the announced interest rate but also by assessing the accessibility of capital, the extent to which it meets production needs, and the efficiency of capital utilization by businesses.

| Nguyễn Tiến Vỵ, a member of SABECO’s Board of Directors, receives the Top 1 Most Reputable Alcoholic Beverage Company 2026 award, announced by Vietnam Report. — Photos courtesy of SABECO | 
HÀ NỘI — Saigon Beer-Alcohol-Beverage Corporation (SABECO) has been named Việt Nam’s most reputable alcoholic beverage company in 2026 by Vietnam Report, maintaining its position at the top of the ranking for several consecutive years.
The ranking reflects the company’s business performance, product innovation and standing among consumers and market stakeholders.
The results were announced at a ceremony in Hà Nội last week, organised by Vietnam Report in collaboration with Vietnamnet newspaper to honour leading companies in the food, beverage, retail, packaging and high-tech agriculture sectors.
According to Vietnam Report, demand for food and beverages is recovering, while consumers are paying greater attention to product quality, safety and origin. These trends are prompting businesses to focus more on product development, supply chain management and building consumer trust.
SABECO ranked first in the alcoholic beverage category based on criteria including financial capacity, media reputation and market credibility, as assessed through surveys of consumers and other stakeholders.
| A beer production line of SABECO. | 
Balancing heritage with product innovation
SABECO draws on more than 150 years of brewing heritage in Việt Nam. The company operates 26 breweries, has a distribution network covering more than 200,000 sales outlets nationwide and exports its products to more than 40 international markets.
Its established brands include Bia Saigon, Bia 333 and Bia Lạc Việt. The company has also expanded its product portfolio to cater to changing consumer preferences.
One recent launch is the limited-edition Bia 333 Triple Pure, which has a lower carbohydrate content and fewer calories, with a smooth, balanced finish. The product is part of the company’s efforts to develop new offerings while maintaining its established brands.
SABECO’s products have also received recognition at international brewing competitions. In 2026, its brands won 25 medals at competitions in the UK, the US and Australia.
At the International Beer Challenge in the UK, SABECO was named Asian Brewer of the Year based on the combined performance of its entries.
Beyond product development, SABECO engages with consumers through food, cultural and sporting events, as well as long-term partnerships.
| Saigon Beer supports the “The Fatherland in Our Hearts” programme, helping foster national pride as Việt Nam marks the 81st anniversary of National Day. | 
Bia Saigon Special has partnered with the Michelin Guide for four consecutive years, linking the brand with Việt Nam’s dining scene. In 2026, Bia Saigon also participated in the Khánh Hòa Sea Festival and the patriotic artistic programme “Tổ Quốc Trong Tim” (The Fatherland in Our Hearts).
In sport, SABECO has supported the Tiền Phong Marathon for six consecutive years. A strategic partnership between Bia Saigon and the Việt Nam Football Federation for 2026-29 is also expected to expand the brand’s engagement with football fans nationwide.
The company has continued to support community welfare programmes. Its 2026 Tết (Lunar New Year) gift-giving campaign delivered 6,500 gift packages to disadvantaged households and border guard forces in border areas, remote regions and coastal communities.
The latest ranking adds to SABECO’s recognition in the domestic beverage market, as the company continues to draw on its brewing heritage while developing products and maintaining engagement with consumers and communities.

TAINAN — Vietjet has launched its direct Hà Nội-Tainan route, further expanding air connectivity between Việt Nam and Taiwan (China), the airline has announced.
It said the new service offers passengers more convenient travel options while contributing to the development of tourism, trade and cultural exchange.
The new route operates four round-trip flights per week, providing convenient connections between the two cities. Through Vietjet’s continuously expanding network, passengers from Tainan can also conveniently connect to destinations across Việt Nam, Southeast Asia, South Asia, Central Asia, Australia and Europe.
Vietjet’s CEO Nguyễn Thanh Sơn said he believed that a flight can shorten geographical distances, while connectivity, mutual understanding and opportunities for shared growth bring people closer together.
"We hope the Hà Nội-Tainan (Taiwan, China) route will become a lasting bridge, helping promote tourism, economic exchange and stronger community ties,” Sơn said.
Since launching its first flight to Taiwan (China) in 2014, Vietjet has carried five million passengers on more than 38,000 flights between Taiwan (China) and Việt Nam. Today, the airline connects Taipei, Taichung, Tainan and Kaohsiung with Hà Nội, HCM City and Phú Quốc, through a total of eight direct routes.
From now through January 2027, the airline will continue to introduce new routes, including Hà Nội/HCM City-Cebu and Clark; Đà Nẵng-Osaka (Kansai); and HCM City-Maldives.
Vietjet said it will also launch the second route to Sydney, serving the newly opened Western Sydney Airport.
| Passengers check in for Vietjet’s inaugural flight from HCM City to Chiang Mai. | 
Resuming the HCM City-Chiang Mai route
Vietjet has also resumed its nonstop service between HCM City and Chiang Mai, operating four round-trip flights per week and offering travellers a convenient new way to explore Northern Thailand. Vietjet is currently the only airline operating nonstop flights on the route.
The route further strengthens air connectivity between Việt Nam and Thailand, supporting tourism, trade and cultural exchange.
From now to November 1, 2026, travellers can take advantage of Vietjet’s special promotion, featuring millions of eco tickets priced from zero dollars (excluding taxes and fees) across Vietjet’s flight network, including the new routes, opening up travel opportunities to destinations throughout Asia and Europe. Tickets are available at www.vietjetair.com and through the Vietjet Air mobile app.
The resumed service further expands the Việt Nam-Thailand network of Vietjet Group’s ecosystem. The network connects major Vietnamese cities, including HCM City, Hà Nội, Đà Nẵng and Phú Quốc, with popular destinations in Thailand such as Bangkok, Phuket and Chiang Mai, while the Thai domestic network provides travellers with more ways to explore destinations across Thailand. — VNS

The immigration management division under the Dong Nai City Police conducted an unannounced inspection of the company as part of efforts to detect and handle foreign nationals residing or working illegally in Vietnam, the municipal police announced on their portal on Sunday.
After reviewing documents and checking the company's actual workforce, inspectors found that the company had failed to fulfill its legal responsibilities when inviting, sponsoring and arranging entry, exit and residence for foreign nationals.
The 91 foreign workers had worked at the company for more than 90 days without work permits or documents confirming that they were exempt from the requirement.
The company was also found to have employed foreign nationals who did not meet the legal requirements.
The inspection team compiled records of administrative violations for handling the company and relevant individuals in accordance with the law.
The case serves as a warning to businesses employing foreign workers that failure to comply with immigration, residence and labor regulations can lead to serious legal consequences and affect labor management and public security.
The immigration management division urged businesses to review the legal documents of all foreign employees and allow them to work only after they have obtained work permits or confirmation that they are exempt from the requirement.
Companies must also fulfill their sponsorship and management responsibilities and promptly notify the authorities of employees leaving their jobs, termination of employment contracts or changes in residence status.
The division said it would continue coordinating with relevant agencies to step up inspections and follow-up checks and strictly handle violations.
2 Bangladeshi nationals overstay in Vietnam, test positive for drugs
Two Bangladeshi nationals who had overstayed their permitted residence in Vietnam tested positive for drugs during an inspection at a guesthouse in Dong Nai City on Saturday night.
At around 10:00 pm, the immigration management division, in coordination with Phuoc Tan Commune Police, conducted an unannounced inspection of H.Q. Guesthouse.
Officers found the two foreign nationals staying at the guesthouse and determined that both had overstayed their permitted residence in Vietnam.
Both individuals also tested positive in rapid on-site drug tests.
Further checks found that the guesthouse owner had failed to declare the two foreign nationals' temporary residence as required by law.
The case is being further investigated for handling in accordance with the law.
26 Chinese nationals working without permits in Da Nang
Authorities in Da Nang City, central Vietnam, have discovered 26 Chinese nationals working without work permits or documents confirming that they are exempt from the requirement at a construction site in Tam Thang 2 Industrial Park.
The municipal immigration management division coordinated with Thang Truong Commune Police to conduct an unannounced inspection at the construction site as part of a campaign to detect and handle violations involving foreign nationals in the city.
The inspection team recorded the case and is continuing to verify the violations involving the individuals and organizations concerned for strict handling in accordance with the law.
The immigration management division said it would continue coordinating with local police and relevant agencies to strengthen inspections of foreign nationals working in the city, promptly detect and handle violations, and improve immigration management to maintain security and public order.
Foreign guests’ temporary residence must be declared even for one-night stays in Vietnam
Vietnam's Ministry of Public Security has reminded accommodation providers that they must declare the temporary residence of foreign guests, including those staying for just one night.
Under Vietnam’s regulations, foreign nationals must have their temporary residence declared through the person directly managing or operating their accommodation.
Before accepting a foreign guest, accommodation providers must ask the guest to present a passport or other valid international travel document and relevant residence papers for verification before making the declaration.
The person responsible for declaring temporary residence is the accommodation's owner, legal representative or an authorized person.
The declaration must be made as soon as the foreign guest arrives, through the ministry's electronic temporary residence declaration system at https://tbltkbtt.bocongan.gov.vn.
If electronic submission is not possible, the responsible person must complete and submit a temporary residence declaration form to the commune-level police.
Accepting bookings through digital platforms does not remove accommodation providers' responsibility to declare foreign guests' temporary residence.
If a foreign guest cannot present a passport or another valid international travel document, or shows signs of violating immigration or residence laws, the accommodation provider must immediately notify the competent authorities.
