Overview
 The directive to lower interest rates to support production and business activities has been fully communicated to the entire credit institution system over the past week.
 To continue implementing solutions to reduce interest rates, contributing to supporting production and business development as directed by the Government and the Prime Minister; based on the conclusions of the Governor of the State Bank of Vietnam at the meeting on October 19, 2026, the State Bank of Vietnam issued Official Letter No. 9736/NHNN-CSTT dated October 21, 2026, instructing commercial banks to resolutely implement the assigned tasks and be responsible before the law , before the Governor of the State Bank of Vietnam and competent authorities for the implementation of the requirements.
 Accordingly, the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) requires commercial banks throughout their systems, across all sales channels, to aggressively implement a substantial reduction in deposit and lending interest rates as directed by the SBV Governor at the meeting on October 19, 2026, and in Official Letter No. 9608/NHNN-CSTT dated October 18, 2026. Commercial banks are required to reduce the average deposit interest rate by at least 0.5% per year for new transactions with maturities of 6 months or more in the last months of 2026 compared to the interest rate of the commercial bank itself in the reporting period from October 11, 2026 to October 20, 2026. On the lending side, the regulatory authority requires banks to focus resources, reduce operating costs, and share profits to lower effective interest rates for customers, prioritizing a 1.5-2 percentage point reduction for loans serving production, business, and priority sectors.
 To ensure that commercial banks seriously implement the State Bank of Vietnam's (SBV) directive on substantially reducing deposit and lending interest rates, the SBV will monitor average interest rate data for new transactions in the last months of 2026 through the statistical reporting system as requested in Official Letter No. 6194/NHNN-DBTK dated August 7, 2023, regarding the requirement to report interest rates on new transactions. In cases where commercial banks fail to comply with the SBV's directive, the SBV will take strict measures, including considering reducing/lowering their credit growth targets.
 Assessing the impact on bank profits, a securities firm estimated that if the portion of outstanding loans subject to a 1.5-2% annual interest rate reduction accounts for approximately 3-5% of the total loan portfolio, the industry's Net Interest Margin (NIM) could decrease by about 0.03-0.07 percentage points, leading to a 2-4% reduction in pre-tax profits. articles.full_text:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is well positioned to play a key role as a regional data centre hub if it can maintain its competitive advantage, Moody’s Ratings said.
It said Malaysia’s competitive advantage stems from competitively priced, readily available power and supportive government initiatives.
Moody's Ratings assistant vice president - ratings Chelsia Ng said the country's policy framework and approval requirements already focus on data centre efficiency, with eligibility for tax incentives under the Digital Ecosystem Acceleration (DESAC) scheme linked to power and water efficiency benchmarks.
"Johor, which houses most of the country’s data centre capacity, also applies more stringent requirements for project approvals.
"These measures should promote more efficient resource use, which should help moderate the incremental pressure on power and water infrastructure as the sector grows,” Ng told Bernama in a recent interview.
Moody’s Ratings estimated that around 14 gigawatts (GW) to 17 GW of additional generation capacity will be required by 2035 to meet the incremental demand in Peninsular Malaysia, which could entail around RM80 billion to RM95 billion of investments to be undertaken by Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) and independent power producers.
Ng noted that data centre-led demand growth would be credit-positive for utilities over the long term, but the elevated capital spending would also entail execution and funding risks and raise financial leverage during the development phase.
She noted that based on government projections, data centres could account for around 31 per cent of total electricity consumption in Peninsular Malaysia by 2035, up from 4.0 per cent in 2025.
"This will underpin structural electricity demand growth, and we expect demand in Peninsular Malaysia to grow at a compound annual rate of around 5.8 per cent over the next decade, although the scale and pace of growth will remain subject to market and execution risks,” said Ng.
She noted that the need for firm baseload capacity to meet data centre power demand would keep gas relevant as a transition fuel, whilst Malaysia continues to scale up solar capacity and battery energy storage systems (BESS) to support system reliability.
Ng said the procurement of new and extended gas-fired capacity under NewGen25 and NewGen26 also underscores the importance of gas in maintaining system reliability as electricity demand rises.
"However, Malaysia will need to balance this requirement (to phase) down coal generation and the need to replace retiring generation capacities over the next decade, which will add another layer of investment and execution risk to the energy transition," she added.
Ng said renewable energy (RE) could also meet part of the additional electricity demand, as solar capacity could be deployed relatively quickly, adding that data centre operators also have their own net-zero and decarbonisation targets, which could drive demand for RE-linked power procurement over time.
Although solar remains a modest contributor to Peninsular Malaysia’s generation mix, she noted that the mandatory inclusion of BESS in the recently launched large-scale solar (LSS) tender programme points to the growing role for solar-plus-storage in meeting incremental demand while supporting Malaysia’s decarbonisation initiatives.
"However, the intermittent nature of renewable generation and current battery storage technologies are unlikely to provide sufficient backup to fully meet data centres’ round-the-clock power requirements in the medium term,” she added.
In June, the government announced that Malaysia will require all future solar power projects under its sixth LSS programme to include BESS, as the government moves to strengthen grid stability alongside RE expansion.
Ng noted that data centre-led demand growth would be credit positive for utilities over the long term, but the elevated capital spending would also entail execution and funding risks and raise financial leverage during the development phase.
"For TNB, annual capital spending is likely to increase to around RM18 billion, driven by higher investment in grid infrastructure and generation capacity.
"Its regulated transmission and distribution investments benefit from a cost-recovery framework which underpins revenue growth,” she added.
Although unregulated generation projects carry greater risk because they take longer to build before generating cash flow, Moody's Ratings expects TNB to have sufficient financial headroom to manage sizable capital spending over the medium term. - Bernama

HÀ NỘI — While savings interest rates have shown signs of cooling down, the rates on certificates of deposit (CDs) have kept rising by 0.1-0.3 percentage points per year.
Following the SBV’s deposit rate cut directive last week, 20 banks have lowered their over-the-counter savings rates for six-month terms by 0.5 percentage points from the October 16 level.
However, the interest rates for CDs have continued to rise.
MB is offering a rate of up to 8 per cent per annum on three-month CDs for deposits of VNĐ300 million or more, 3.25 percentage points higher than the rate for a standard savings account of the same term. For deposits of VNĐ1 billion or more, the annual rate can reach 9.4 per cent.
Similarly, VPBank is offering CD rates of up to 9 per cent per annum, while BVBank provides a maximum rate of 8.2 per cent per annum for terms ranging from six to 12 months.
The high CD rates showed that competitive pressure to attract capital remains, even as the general level of savings interest rates trends downward.
During the first nine months of 2026, many banks ramped up capital raising through CDs.
According to its third-quarter 2026 financial report, Techcombank’s outstanding balance of certificates of deposit reached VNĐ186.27 trillion, up 18.2 per cent from the end of 2025.
Of this total, CDs issued to individual customers amounted to more than VNĐ100.45 trillion, up 7.7 per cent from the end of the previous year and accounting for approximately 53.9 per cent of the bank’s total CD balance.
During the same period, VPBank’s outstanding balance of CDs reached VNĐ160.91 trillion, an increase of 153.6 per cent, compared to the end of 2025. Of the total, CDs issued to individual customers saw a sharp rise of 88.7 per cent, climbing from VNĐ26.30 trillion to VNĐ49.64 trillion.
According to its third-quarter 2026 financial report, LPBank recorded an outstanding CD balance of VNĐ65.85 trillion as of September 30, 2026. This represented an 81.6 per cent increase from the VNĐ36.25 trillion recorded at the end of 2025.
At ABBank, the balance of CDs also reached VNĐ23.39 trillion by the end of September 2026, a 72 per cent increase from the VNĐ13.6 trillion recorded at the end of 2025.
Trương Đắc Nguyên, founder of investment firm Trương Nguyên, noted diverging interest rate trends across various deposit products.
While interest rates for standard savings accounts have edged downward, rates for other channels have continued to rise, signaling that banks remain driven by a need to secure capital, even at a higher cost.
Echoing this view, experts at SSI Research anticipated that the issuance of CDs and bonds will continue to accelerate, serving as an additional tool to help narrow the gap between credit growth and deposit mobilisation.
This shift indicated that banks are increasingly raising capital through longer-term instruments, which can help stabilise their funding bases and support the expansion of medium- and long-term credit.
However, a heavy reliance on CDs, particularly those with longer tenors, could also drive up the cost of capital if the issuance rates exceed those of conventional deposit products. — BIZHUB/VNS

Justice Yusrin Faidz Yusoff dismissed Nur Nabilah Ahmad Zambala’s appeal, ruling that although the school had no express authority under its examination rules to inspect the contents of her phone, the procedural irregularity did not establish actionable negligence.
The Form 5 student was searched after two students reported seeing her looking at a phone during a Home Science trial examination at SMK Sura in Dungun on Oct 25, 2020.
The phone was examined by the school principal and subject teachers, who found notes and answer schemes corresponding to answers in her scripts for several subjects.
The school reduced her marks for the affected papers to 1%, although the marks were restored following intervention by the district education office.
Nabilah sued for damages over alleged humiliation, emotional distress and damage to her reputation.
She claimed the school acted negligently and defamed her by writing “meniru paper SnRT” (cheated in the Home Science paper) on the envelope containing her phone.
However, Yusrin ruled that the words were not defamatory in their context and that the defendants had established the defence of justification by proving the substantial truth of the allegation.
He said the school’s internal communication was also protected by qualified privilege.
The judge said the school’s inspection of the phone exceeded the authority expressly provided for under its circular and examination rules, but the evidence remained admissible, albeit with reduced weight.
He also expressed concern that the school failed to refer the suspected leak of confidential trial examination papers to the relevant education authorities.
In dismissing the appeal, Yusrin affirmed the sessions court’s decision and ordered Nabilah to pay RM5,000 in appeal costs, in addition to the RM10,000 awarded in costs by the lower court.
The judge said Nabilah failed to establish her claims on a balance of probabilities and that the defendants had not been negligent.
“The appellant’s own actions were the primary cause of her predicament,” he said, adding that she had chosen to bring a phone into the examination hall despite knowing it was prohibited.
“She cannot now complain about the consequences of her own actions.”
Yusrin noted in his judgment that Nabilah was a school prefect who had represented the school and Terengganu in various national and international scouting events.
Her parents were teachers when the suit was filed in 2021.
Hisyam Yusof and Nor Fatihah Hazmira Mat Azmi appeared for Nabilah while federal counsel Nik Rabiatul Adawiah Soupy and Faizuan Khalid represented the government.

The South Sumatra station of the meteorology, climatology and geophysics agency (BMKG) expects the rainy season to begin in November, though its Jakarta-based weather forecasters have said some fire-prone areas could see it arrive in October.
In the meantime, scattered showers have begun falling across Sumatra and Kalimantan, with some rain induced by cloud seeding.
The return of rain following cloud-seeding operations is encouraging, as the technique requires suitable clouds to be present.

BMKG’s South Sumatra station expects October rain to stay relatively light, with the rainy season setting in across the province in November.
South Sumatra has endured a dry season lasting more than four months, with some areas going more than 100 days without rain.
BMKG still lists South Sumatra, Jambi, Bengkulu, Lampung and Bangka Belitung as provinces at risk of fires through Oct 31.
Riau province entered its rainy season in September, helping to reduce the number of hotspots, BMKG said.
BMKG also said in September that the southern parts of Central and West Kalimantan would enter the rainy season in October. Its Palangka Raya station forecasts rain in the city from Oct 27 to 30.
But relief cannot come soon enough. On Oct 25, visibility in parts of the city fell to about 50m as haze thickened, local media reported.
South Kalimantan’s climate station expects below-normal rainfall through the end of October. In East Kalimantan, the rainy season is forecast to begin in western and central areas in late October, and in most other areas by mid-November.
The ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre has said more showers during the inter-monsoon period towards the end of October could begin to ease the hotspot and haze situation across the region.
Forest fires across Indonesia, particularly on the islands of Sumatra and Kalimantan, have been exacerbated by a strong 2026 El Nino weather phenomenon, sending haze across the region.

Mum confronts headmaster over alleged ‘I love you’ texts to 15-year-old daughter, lunges at him as he pleads forgiveness
A video showing a mother angrily confronting a secondary school headmaster in Perak, Malaysia, has gone viral following allegations that he sent inappropriate messages to her 15-year-old daughter.
The footage, which is circulating on a popular Malaysian subreddit, shows the mother confronting the headmaster in his office, accompanied by another woman clad in a pink top.
The headmaster puts his palms together, appearing to plead for forgiveness as the mother continues to express her anger.
At one point, she hits him on the arm before lunging towards him, with the other woman stepping in to restrain her.
According to Malaysian media reports, the confrontation was reportedly sparked by allegations that the headmaster had sent the girl text messages including one that said “I love you”.
The allegations were also raised in a post on Threads, which also accused the headmaster of sexual harassment.
The Reddit thread has amassed at least 440 upvotes and 56 comments, including one that showed a certificate of the man’s appointment as headmaster.
Headmaster temporarily transferred pending investigation
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said she had directed Perak’s education department to look into the matter, according to The New Straits Times (NST).
“The headmaster involved has also been temporarily moved to the Bagan Datuk district education office pending the completion of the investigation,” she said.
Located in Perak, Bagan Datuk is about 40 kilometres away from Teluk Intan, the district where the headmaster worked in before the probe.
The viral Threads post also called on authorities to take the matter seriously and ensure students’ safety.
However, Bagan Datuk district police chief Mohamad Ali said police had not received a report about the incident, according to a Sin Chew Daily report.
